question: LOKI_SIMPLE=1 cuts the assembled prompt 78%. That is a TOKEN measurement. Does the stripped arm still build the thing, and does it take more or fewer iterations?
method: benchmarks/run-prompt-ablation.sh, 5 trials per arm. ONE engine copy, same spec, model (sonnet), caps and machine -- the arms differ by a single environment variable read at prompt-assembly time. The engine stamps prompt_arm from its OWN environment and the harness refuses to record a trial whose stamp disagrees with the harness label. Acceptance is an artifact check (greet.js_exists), not a self-report.

result.acceptance: 5/5 in BOTH arms -- no regression from stripping the prompt
result.act_iterations: 1 in every run of both arms -- no change

the_n3_trap: AT n=3 THIS DATASET LOOKED LIKE AN 18% SPEEDUP WITH PERFECT SEPARATION. The first three simple trials were 415, 419, 450s against full's 462, 493, 532s -- every simple run beat every full run. The design floor at n=3/3 is p=0.1, so the analyser reported UNDERPOWERED and no claim was published. Trials 4 and 5 came in at 506 and 1330s and the separation vanished entirely: p rose to 0.5714 with a floor of 0.0079, meaning the test had ample power and found nothing. Had the floor been ignored at n=3, this repository would have shipped a false 18% speed claim.
actual_finding: The stripped prompt is not faster. It is MORE VARIABLE. Full arm spread 95s over 5 runs (stdev 32.6s); simple arm spread 915s (stdev 354.5s) -- 9.6x wider, with a tail run at 2.96x its own median. The coaching prompt appears to buy predictability rather than speed. This is a hypothesis generated by 5 trials per arm, not an established result: a variance claim needs more data than a location claim.
verdict: SAFE ON OUTCOMES, NO SPEED BENEFIT MEASURED. LOKI_SIMPLE=1 completed 5/5 in one iteration each, identical to the full prompt. No wall-clock advantage survives n=5.
not_claimed: No multiplier is reported. The 78% prompt reduction is a TOKEN measurement and says nothing about outcomes; only the acceptance and iteration results below speak to behaviour. Arms differ by one environment variable in one binary on one machine -- nothing here compares Loki to another vendor.
